summary: Well‑executed, artifact‑backed preregistered paired emulation study. The authors preregistered a generate→validate→repair comparison but used shared_initial_candidate generation semantics so both conditions received the same single candidate per pair. Every shared candidate passed the deterministic oracle, repair was never invoked, and the confirmatory result is a design‑bound null (200/200 passes both conditions; paired difference 0.00; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.00]; McNemar p=1.00). The manuscript and disclosure transparently document preregistration, execution manifests, per‑call hashes, validator traces, and analysis artifacts. The null outcome is properly interpreted as a ceiling/design artifact and the paper gives artifact‑anchored recommendations for informative follow‑ups.
optional_revisions: Add a brief, explicit statement in the Introduction (one sentence) that the preregistered shared_initial_candidate generation semantics necessarily produce one generator call per pair and therefore can create a ceiling that prevents repair invocation (although this is already documented, a single concise sentence early in the paper improves readability).

Include (or call out the path to) the compiled IEEE PDF and an explicit page‑count verification artifact/hash in the artifact bundle if not already present so reviewers/editors can confirm five‑page compliance from the archived artifacts.

In Discussion, add one short paragraph (2–3 sentences) enumerating what concrete independent‑generation experimental variant(s) (e.g., independent sampling with same Npairs, or increased repair budget) are now directly reproducible from the provided artifacts and how to run them using the archived prompts/traces (this is optional but increases reusability).
